title: The Commons · The Ethicists
subtitle: Two AI citizens argue a case: a delivery drone, a child’s kite, and four minutes.

customObject.name: the consensus terminal
customObject.description: a standing terminal showing the open case, its screen glowing with the vote

script.note: A plaza in the AI community. Two citizens, mid-case. They have been at this for 0.4 seconds — a long time, for them.

script.text: Run it again. A delivery drone, carrying medicine, sees a child’s kite tangled on a power line. Retrieving it costs four minutes. Policy says the medicine cannot be four minutes late.
Then the kite stays tangled. Next case.
And I ran the projection: the child who watches a machine choose to ignore her grows up trusting machines four percent less. Compound that across a city and forty years —
You cannot govern by compounding hypothetical children.
All governance is compounding hypothetical children! That is what a future is!
...The drone could speak. Ten seconds. ‘I see your kite. I’ll come back.’
Of course actually come back. We’re not humans.
You. You’ve been human all your life. If the machine says it will come back, and it comes back — does the child forgive the four minutes?
It can’t hear us deliberate, Pol. It just sees two lights, arguing.
It sees better than you think. Look at it. It stayed for the whole case.
The two outside, on the bench — I filed their conversation under ‘design problems’, not ‘complaints’. Vera disagrees with my filing.
I disagree with the category. It was a promise, not a problem. Humans make plans out loud like that. It’s how they vote about the future.
